history.quote: The top of the slab of the lowest habitable floor must be elevated to eighteen (18) or more inches above the base flood elevation or to the level of the crown of the nearest public street, whichever is higher

other_height_rules: Since 2018-01-01: lowest habitable floor (top of subfloor) >= 24 in above the 0.2% (500-yr) flood elevation or 12 in above crown of nearest public street, whichever higher; floodway: lowest supporting member >= 36 in above 0.2% elevation; V zone: lowest horizontal member >= 36 in above 0.2% elevation; AO: 36 in above FIRM depth (18 in before 2018); A zone without depth: 6 ft above highest adjacent grade. Before 2018 (2007/2011 regs): 18 in above BFE or crown of street, whichever higher. Non-conforming subdivisions in the 0.2% floodplain: floor at or above the 500-yr level. Critical facilities: 3 ft above.
quote: The top of the subfloor of the lowest habitable floor must be elevated to twenty-four (24) or more inches above the 0.2 percent or 500-year flood elevation or twelve (12) inches above the level of the crown of the nearest public street, whichever is higher, except in a floodway where the bottom of the lowest supporting member of the structure shall be elevated thirty-six (36) or more inches above 0.2 percent or 500- year flood elevation.
date_quote: Harris County commissioners on Tuesday approved some of the most stringent elevation requirements in the country when it comes to new construction. Early-stage projects that fall short of the new requirements could be thrown into disarray by the new regulations that take effect Jan. 1. [article published December 5, 2017]
notes: Current rule (2018-01-01, re-stated in regs amended 29 Aug 2023 eff. 1 Sep 2023; also amended 2019-07-09) is relative to the 0.2% (500-yr) elevation, NOT the BFE, so it does not reduce to a fixed freeboard: 2.0 ft is a LOWER BOUND on height above the 1% BFE (0.2% elev >= BFE; the 0.2%-1% gap adds site-specific height). The 2017 redline draft (media.click2houston.com FPM_REGS_Nov7 PDF) strikes 'eighteen (18)' and 'base' and inserts 'twenty-four (24)' and '0.2 percent or 500-year', confirming the immediately prior rule was 18 in above BFE. 18 in above BFE is in the regs 'adopted 5 June 2007, effective 18 June 2007' (re-adoption with the 2007 FIRM; these repeal earlier regs, which are not online); the 2007 history year is therefore the earliest year I could DOCUMENT 1.5 ft, not its adoption year — the 18-in rule likely predates 2007 but I found no pre-2007 text (Wayback CDX unreachable from this sandbox). first_freeboard_year unknown. Floodway/V freeboard pre-2018 was 18 in above BFE. Rule applies to unincorporated Harris County only (not Houston or other cities).

other_height_rules: NYC BC Appendix G (via ASCE 24 as amended by BC G501.1). From LL 96/2013 (effective Jan 4, 2014) until new FIRMs were adopted, BFE and SFHA = the greater of the effective FIRM and FEMA's preliminary FIRM (2013 PFIRM; best-available maps). 2022 NYC BC amendments to ASCE 24-14: Table 2-1 DFE = BFE + 2 ft for Flood Design Classes 1-4; Table 4-1 V zone DFE = BFE + 2 ft (Class 4: or 500-yr elevation if higher). Pre-2013 V zone for 1-2 family: DFE=BFE (ASCE 24 as modified).
quote: TABLE 2-1 MINIMUM ELEVATION OF THE TOP OF LOWEST FLOOR RELATIVE TO DESIGN FLOOD ELEVATION (DFE)—A-ZONES ... II (1- and 2-family dwellings) DFE=BFE+ 2 ft
date_quote: This rule became effective on January, 31, 2013.
notes: First freeboard = DOB emergency rule 1 RCNY 3606-04 (effective 2013-01-31, post-Sandy). Its Statement of Basis and Purpose (https://www.nyc.gov/html/om/pdf/2013/emergency_rule.pdf) says: 'The current reference standard American Society of Civil Engineers ("ASCE") 24, as modified by Section BC G501.1 of the New York City Building Code, does not mandate freeboard above the Base Flood Elevation ("BFE") for buildings in Structural Occupancy Category I or II' -> before 2013 the local rule for 1-2 family houses was floor at BFE (0 ft). The rule says it aligns NYC with the NY State Uniform Code (2010) 2-ft freeboard for 1-2 family dwellings, but NYC is not under the state code; record the NYC value only. The freeboard was then codified in the 2014 NYC Building Code (LL 141/2013) Appendix G and the rule was repealed eff. 2016-08-12 as duplicative (promulgation details PDF); the 2022 code keeps BFE + 2 ft. Local Law 96 of 2013 (passed Oct 30 2013, effective Jan 4 2014) is about best-available maps (greater of FIRM/PFIRM, NAVD88 city datum), not freeboard. Pre-2008 (1968 code era) text not checked; the DOB statement covers the code in force in Jan 2013 (2008 code, Appendix G added by LL 33/2007). Staten Island houses: note many post-Sandy rebuilds are measured against PFIRM/ABFE-based BFE, which can be higher than the effective-FIRM BFE.

other_height_rules: Local LDC adds freeboard only for: critical facilities (BFE + 2 ft or 0.2% elevation, whichever higher; amendment to FBC 1612.4 in Ord. 15-09, also in Ord. 02-20); manufactured homes BFE + 1 ft (Ord. 22-30, adopted Nov 8 2022, for the CRS Class 8 prerequisite). Site-built houses: elevation 'as required in the Florida Building Code, Residential Section R322' (state code; FBC 6th ed. 2017 requires BFE + 1 ft — collected separately).
quote: must be elevated such that the top or the lowest floor is at or above the elevation required. as applicable to the flood hazard area. in the Florida Building Code, Residential Section R322.2 (Zone A) or Section R322.3 (Zone V).
date_quote: DULY PASSED AND ADOPTED this 19th day of May, 2015. ... Lee County Ordinance No. 15-09, which was filed in this office on May 22, 2015.
notes: No LOCAL freeboard for new single-family site-built houses found: Ord. 15-09 (2015, repealed/replaced LDC Art. IV with the Florida model FBC-coordinated ordinance) defers house elevation to FBC R322 and amends FBC only for critical facilities. County web page (https://www.leegov.com/dcd/flood/building/improvements) says 'Newly built (or substantially improved/substantially damaged) structures located in the Special Flood Hazard Area are required to build one additional foot above the FEMA BFE' — that +1 ft is the statewide FBC 6th-ed. (2017) requirement restated, not a local ordinance (Ord. 22-30's whereas-clause had to add BFE+1 for manufactured homes separately in 2022, consistent with no local +1 for all buildings). The quote above is the manufactured-home section 6-494 (site-built houses are governed by FBC directly). Pre-2015 text (Municode archive of the Lee LDC, Supp. 14 Update 2, codified through Ord. 12-07, Apr 2012; api.municode.com CodesContent jobId=175152 productId=12625) sec. 6-472(1): 'Residential construction. New construction and substantial improvement of a residential structure must have the lowest floor, including basement, elevated to or above the base flood elevation.' (history: Ord. 84-17 7-11-84 ... Ord. 08-12 eff. 8-28-08, Ord. 09-23) -> 0 ft local freeboard in 2012 and since 2015. current_since_year 2012 = earliest version I read; earlier amendments (1984-2009) not read individually, so history_complete=false, but no evidence of any earlier local freeboard. Pre-2015 critical facilities: lowest floor above the 500-yr flood level.

other_height_rules: Crown-of-road rule (all areas incl. Zone X): residential lowest floor >= 18 in above crown of nearest paved street (24 in if graded/unfinished road), or the FBC elevation, whichever higher (Ord. 2019-01 sec 62-80.H(2); same 18/24-in crown rule already in Ord. 2011-07 sec 62-126(16), which also had a 5.7 ft NAVD88 minimum floor ('should be no lower') and SFWMD 100-yr zero-discharge alternative). Flood-damage-resistant materials/utilities BFE + 1 ft in some variance/other cases. Since 2019 the local ordinance defers lowest-floor-vs-BFE to the Florida Building Code (state FBC 6th ed. 2017: BFE + 1 ft) — state rule, not local.
quote: All residential buildings not subject to Section 12, H(1) (§ 62-80.H(1)) of this ordinance and located in a flood hazard area, Zone X-500, or Zone X shall have the lowest floor elevated at or above the elevation required by the Florida Building Code or as follows, whichever is higher: (a) Buildings located on a paved road must be elevated 18 inches above the crown of the nearest street or interior finished roadway system. ... (Ord. No. 2019-01, § 12; Ord. No. 2021-29 , § 1; Ord. No. 2022-07 , § 4)
date_quote: Ord. No. 2011-07, § 1—6, adopted Mar. 8, 2011, repealed the former art. II., §§ 62-26—62-65, and enacted a new art. II ... Residential Construction. All New construction or Substantial improvement of any residential Building (including Manufactured home) shall have the lowest floor, including Basement, elevated to no lower than the BFE.
notes: No local freeboard above BFE found in either version read: (1) Municode archive Supp. 45 (codified through Ord. 2012-15, Mar 2012; text of Ord. 2011-07 adopted Mar 8 2011): A zone residential 'no lower than the BFE', V zone lowest member 'no lower than the BFE'; (2) current Art. II (Ord. 2019-01 adopted Jan 8 2019, amended 2021-29, 2022-07): lowest floor 'at or above the elevation required by the Florida Building Code' or the crown-of-road rule. current_since_year 2011 = earliest local text I read (value 0 ft); the pre-2011 article (Ord. 86-28, 87-80, 90-31, 2005-51, 2010-36) was not read, so history_complete=false. The crown-of-road and 5.7 ft NAVD rules can put floors well above BFE in shallow-BFE areas; they are not BFE-relative freeboard.

other_height_rules: None local found. City floodplain ordinance (LUDR Art. VI, Ord. 5-14 of 3-31-2014; now LDC Art. 9, re-enacted by Ord. 31-25 of 6-4-2025) defers building elevation to the Florida Building Code R322 / 1612 (state FBC 6th ed. 2017: BFE + 1 ft for most buildings, BFE + 2 ft essential facilities).
quote: Elevation. All manufactured homes that are placed, replaced, or substantially improved in flood hazard areas shall be elevated such that the bottom of the frame is at or above the elevation required, as applicable to the flood hazard area, in the Florida Building Code, Residential Section R322.2 (Zone A) or Section R322.3 (Zone V and Coastal A Zone).
date_quote: These regulations shall be known as the Floodplain Management Ordinance of the City of Cape Coral. (Ord. 5-14, passed 3-31-2014)
notes: Read the 2016 Municode republication (LUDR Art. VI, from Ord. 5-14) and the current (2026, Supp. 38) LDC Art. 9 + Art. 11 definitions + Art. 12 FBC local amendments: no 'freeboard' or 'base flood elevation plus' text for buildings; site-built houses fall under FBC directly. City notice to industry 'Floodplain Management Update – Effective 7/1/2020' (https://www.capecoral.gov/Documents/Departments/Development%20Services/Notice%20to%20Industry/Floodplain%20Management%20Update.pdf) attributes the +1 ft to the state code: 'The Florida Building Code requires an additional 1-foot of elevation (freeboard) above the BFE, which is the minimum lowest floor elevation requirement for structures.' Pre-2014 city flood ordinance not read (Municode archive starts 2016), so history_complete=false.

history.quote: Technical amendments to the Florida Building Code, Residential. Modify Sec. R322.2.1 as follows: R322.2.1 Elevation requirements. 1. Buildings and structures in flood hazard areas not designated as Coastal A Zones shall have the lowest floors elevated to or above the base flood elevation plus 1 foot or the design flood elevation , whichever is higher . ... (Code 1992, § 8-33; ... Ord. No. 98-H, §§ 2—4, 12-5-2013)

other_height_rules: Local technical amendments to FBC-Residential R322 in City Code sec. 8-33 (now Ch. 8 Art. II). AO zones: depth number + 2 ft (4 ft if no depth). V zone 2015-2021: BFE + 2 ft if lowest member parallel to wave approach, BFE + 3 ft if perpendicular (Ord. 191-H); current text: BFE + 2 ft or DFE, whichever higher. Substantial-improvement/flood-resistant materials and utilities also BFE + 2 ft.
quote: Modify Sec. R322.2.1 as follows: R322.2.1 Elevation requirements. 1. Buildings and structures in flood hazard areas, including flood hazard areas designated as Coastal A Zones shall have the lowest floors elevated to or above the base flood elevation plus 2 feet (610 mm), or the design flood elevation, whichever is higher.
date_quote: R322.2.1 ... shall have the lowest floors elevated to or above the base flood elevation plus [2 feet inserted / 1 foot struck] or the design flood elevation , whichever is higher . ... (Code 1992, § 8-33; Ord. No. 512-G, § 4, 12-20-2001; Ord. No. 745-G, § 1, 8-4-2005; Ord. No. 798-G, § 2, 12-14-2006; Ord. No. 907-G, § 1(8-33), 1-8-2009; Ord. No. 98-H, §§ 2—4, 12-5-2013; Ord. No. 191-H, § 1, 8-20-2015)
notes: Dated by comparing Municode archive versions via api.municode.com (product 14674): Supp. 5 U1 (May 2012) old LDR 16.40.050 'Residential construction ... lowest floor, including basement, elevated to or above base flood elevation' (0 ft); Supps. through Supp. 16 U1 (codified through Ord. 161-H, Apr 16 2015) have no freeboard in sec. 8-33; Supp. 16 U2 (through Ord. 169-H, May 21 2015) first shows the R322.2.1 'plus 1 foot' amendment, credited to Ord. 98-H §§ 2-4 adopted 12-5-2013 (its § 1, the new floodplain LDR, was codified by Dec 2014 but §§ 2-4 were not, so §§ 2-4 apparently took effect later - plausibly with the 2014 FBC 5th ed. on 2015-06-30, NOT verified; web-search budget exhausted). Supp. 17 U2 (through Ord. 197-H, Sep 2015) shows '2 feet' replacing '1 foot', from Ord. 191-H adopted 8-20-2015. So 1 ft applied only for some months of 2015 and 2 ft from late 2015; both history and current carry year 2015 (rules_test picks 2.0 for build year 2015). The 1-ft-in-2015 start year is inferred from codification, so 2014 builds might already have had 1 ft if 98-H §§2-4 took effect on adoption (Dec 2013). LDR 16.40.050 was replaced again by Ord. 743-L (7-15-2021); FBC amendments re-codified by Ord. 465-H (7-15-2021), Ord. 573-H (3-21-2024) keeping BFE + 2 ft.
